papers.title_en: NeuroMotion: Aligning EEG to Discrete Motion Primitives for Continuous Motion Decoding
papers.authors: Yi Liu, Qi Zhang, HaoLin Li, Lai Zhong Yuan, Lei Zhu, Heng Tao Shen
papers.evidence: 基于VQ运动原语和Transformer的EEG到运动解码用于连续BCI控制
papers.tldr: 针对噪声头皮EEG难以直接映射到连续运动的问题，提出NeuroMotion框架，通过VQ运动先验将连续运动离散化为原语，并对齐EEG表示与原语进行原型和对比学习，再经E2M Transformer预测运动码序列及几何细化，实现跨全身、下肢和上肢范式的连续运动解码，在三个数据集上取得最佳重建性能。
papers.abstract_en: EEG-to-motion decoding remains challenging because noisy scalp EEG is difficult to map directly to continuous kinematics. We present NeuroMotion, a framework that aligns EEG representations to discrete motion primitives for continuous motion decoding across heterogeneous paradigms, including full-body free movement, lower-limb treadmill locomotion, and upper-limb freewill reaching and grasping. A VQ-based motion prior discretizes continuous motion into reusable primitives that serve as both alignment prototypes and intermediate prediction targets. Prototypical and supervised contrastive objectives align EEG embeddings to motion-derived prototypes and organize them according to primitive assignments. An E2M Transformer predicts motion-code sequences from the learned EEG representations, while a final geometric refinement stage improves continuous trajectory reconstruction through motion-level training. Under a last-session test protocol, NeuroMotion achieves the best mean reconstruction performance among the compared EEG decoding baselines across all three datasets, with the clearest gains on full-body motion in both reconstruction accuracy and distribution-level quality. Multi-subject ablations further support the contributions of EEG-to-primitive alignment, token prediction, and refinement. Code is available at https://github.com/Liuyi2351433/NeuroAction.

papers.title_en: EEG Decoding in Context: A Framework for Tuning-Free EEG Foundation Models
papers.authors: Hao-Run Cai, Si-Yang Liu, Han-Jia Ye, Hairong Zheng
papers.evidence: 基于上下文学习的无需参数更新的脑机接口脑电解码
papers.tldr: 本文针对现有EEG基础模型仍需任务特定解码器和梯度微调的问题，研究基于上下文学习的免调优范式。通过将标注EEG记录作为上下文，结合EEG特定上下文构造、冻结的上下文预测器和基于度量的上下文适应机制，使新记录无需参数更新即可预测。在10个数据集7种范式上取得最高平均BAcc，为免调优EEG基础模型提供实用路径。
papers.abstract_en: Electroencephalography (EEG) decoding is a central route toward brain-computer interfaces for communication, rehabilitation, cognitive assessment, and neurological monitoring. Recent EEG foundation models have substantially advanced reusable signal representations, but their downstream use still typically requires a task-specific decoder, gradient-based adaptation, and validation-driven model selection. We investigate a complementary foundation-model paradigm based on in-context learning: labeled EEG recordings define the decoding task as context, and new recordings are predicted without updating model parameters. We first pair raw EEG features with a pretrained general-purpose in-context predictor. This direct formulation provides a promising starting point, but its performance remains limited and unstable and does not generalize reliably across EEG paradigms. We find that suitable context construction can address these limitations by improving the effective signal-to-noise ratio and exposing temporal and spatial structure. Building on this insight, we introduce a general framework that combines EEG-specific context construction with a frozen in-context predictor and a metric-based context adaptation mechanism, which matches each downstream task to an appropriate context representation without relying on validation data. Across ten datasets spanning seven EEG decoding paradigms, our method achieves the highest mean BAcc among eleven specialized and fine-tuned EEG baselines, without task-specific parameter updates or validation-based model selection. This framework provides a practical path toward tuning-free EEG foundation models in which adaptation is expressed through context rather than parameter updates.

papers.title_en: Reconstructing Natural Images from Brain Activity during Natural Vision
papers.authors: Tejasvi Kothapalli, Ryan Ressmeyer, Declan Rowley, Gregory D. Horwitz, Jude Mitchell, Alexander C. Huk, Bruno Olshausen, Jacob Yates
papers.evidence: 从自然视觉脑活动重建自然图像
papers.tldr: 本文提出在灵长类动物自由观看自然场景时，利用LGN和V1高密度电极阵列记录神经活动，结合眼动信息重建完整图像。通过线性1/f先验方法和深度学习（脉冲token化、Transformer与扩散模型）实现解码，重建质量受神经证据量、眼动追踪精度和图像先验影响，在fMRI、EEG、MEG和电生理等多种脑记录模态中达到新最优性能。
papers.abstract_en: Reconstructing images from brain activity has two broad goals. The first is to build brain-computer interfaces. The second is to understand how the brain sees. The eyes deliver incomplete, noisy input, so the brain must fill in the gaps with its expectations of what natural scenes look like. This filling-in relies on the brain's prior over natural images. Image reconstruction lets us test which natural image prior best matches the brain's natural image prior. However, most previous work on image reconstruction relies on an unnatural condition: subjects must hold their eyes still. In reality, primates constantly move their eyes to see the world. We introduce a framework for reconstructing images from neural activity while a primate freely views a static natural scene. We record from five monkeys with high-density electrode arrays in the lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN) and primary visual cortex (V1). The recorded receptive fields cover only a small part of the image. Thus, we combine neural activity across eye movements, trials, and sessions to reconstruct the full image. We first present a simple linear method with a 1/f prior. We then scale this approach up with modern deep learning. We train a decoder by tokenizing spiking activity and measured gaze; these tokens are fed into a transformer and diffusion model to reconstruct the full scene. Three factors determine reconstruction quality: the amount of neural evidence combined over viewing time, the accuracy of eye tracking, and the choice of image prior. Our method sets a new state-of-the-art performance in reconstructing natural images from brain activity, across brain recording modalities: fMRI, EEG, MEG and electrophysiology.

papers.title_en: PFedHASNet: A Personalized Federated Hybrid Analog-Spike Network for Multi-Subject Motor Imagery EEG Decoding
papers.authors: Peijia Li, Ruidong Ma, Xianghong Lin, Xiangwen Wang, Guoyong Shi, Shuai Huang, Hongqi Li
papers.evidence: 基于联邦混合网络的运动想象脑电解码用于脑机接口
papers.tldr: 针对多受试者运动想象脑电图数据分散、标注成本高且集中训练存在隐私风险的问题，提出个性化联邦混合模拟-脉冲网络PFedHASNet。该网络在联邦学习框架下，共享编码器融合连续时间特征、LIF脉冲响应和通道对数方差，客户端私有残差适配器和分类器实现个性化预测。在四个公开数据集上取得最优平均客户端宏观F1，模型紧凑且性能有竞争力。
papers.abstract_en: Motor imagery electroencephalography (MI-EEG) data are often collected and stored separately across subjects or institutions, and EEG acquisition and annotation remain costly. Training models solely on individual subject data limits the use of information from other subjects, whereas centralizing raw EEG recordings raises privacy and data governance concerns. Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed clients without sharing raw EEG data, providing a practical approach to leveraging information from multiple subjects. Accordingly, we propose PFedHASNet, a personalized federated hybrid analog-spike network for MI-EEG decoding. The shared encoder integrates continuous-valued temporal features, leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) spike responses, and channel-wise log-variance statistics through learnable fusion weights. Client-private residual adapters and classifiers perform subject-specific feature refinement and personalized prediction, respectively. Experiments on held-out trials from participating subjects across four public MI-EEG datasets show that PFedHASNet achieves the highest mean client macro-F1 among 18 model configurations in cross-model comparisons, while maintaining competitive decoding performance with a compact client-side model in comparisons using the same backbone. Ablation studies further examine the contributions of hybrid representations and personalization components to decoding performance.

papers.title_en: EEGJev: A System One Decision Model and Benchmark for Multi-Task EEG Question Answering
papers.evidence: 对神经记录进行多任务脑电解码问答
papers.tldr: 针对单次EEG记录支持多解码任务但固定标签测试无法评估模型对动态问题的适应性问题，本文提出EEGJev快速决策模型，一次通过评分候选答案，并构建涵盖19个公共EEG来源、六类问题的EEGJev-Bench基准。在13个测试源上，属性选择准确率达99.70%，答案平衡准确率62.04%，响应快于NeuroLM。该工作支持通过改问题切换解码目标，为多任务EEG问答提供新评估框架。
papers.abstract_en: A single electroencephalographic (EEG) recording can support multiple decoding tasks. Fixed-label tests cannot show how EEG foundation models handle changing questions or options. We introduce EEGJev, a fast decision model that scores candidate answers in one pass. Our benchmark, EEGJev-Bench, covers six question types across 19 public EEG sources. We held the recording and options fixed while switching between questions about attributes paired during training, such as facial expression and the hand participants were asked to use. Across 13 test sources, EEGJev selected a label for the requested attribute with 99.70% accuracy (49.20% under uniform choice). Balanced accuracy for the specific answer was 62.04%. Its 95th-percentile response time was shorter than NeuroLM's on matched validation questions answered individually. EEGJev lets users switch decoding targets by changing the question. With EEGJev-Bench, researchers can test whether new decoders follow the question more reliably, identify the correct answer more often, or both.

papers.title_en: EEG-World: Context-Conditioned Dynamics of the Watching Brain
papers.authors: Junxiang Zhang, Jiayu Zuo, Wenhao Ye, Junfeng Xia, Xiang Chen, Mo Wang, Quanying Liu
papers.evidence: 从视听输入和先前脑电预测脑电频带功率动态
papers.tldr: 现有脑编码模型常忽略个体持续脑活动对神经反应的影响。本文提出 EEG-World，一个循环世界模型，利用6秒先前 EEG 与后续视听刺激预测未来10秒 EEG 频带功率动态。在78人2584小时数据上，模型非线性预测超越线性基线，预测相关性达0.261，迁移到新个体23/24优于基线，并分离出刺激依赖成分，验证了视觉表征。为个体化 EEG 预测提供了新思路。
papers.abstract_en: Brain encoding models predict neural responses from audiovisual input, but typically overlook how ongoing brain activity shapes an individual's response. We introduce EEG-World, a recurrent world model that forecasts 10 seconds of EEG band-power dynamics from 6 seconds of preceding EEG and the subsequent audiovisual stimulus. Pretrained on continuous EEG, EEG-World learns shared neural dynamics and adapts to unseen individuals through lightweight subject-specific readouts. Using 2,584 hours of EEG from 78 participants, we show that nonlinear recurrent forecasting surpasses strong history-aware linear baselines at scale. EEG-World achieves a forecasting correlation of 0.261 versus 0.233 for the strongest history-and-video linear model, with a 3.3-second forecasting-horizon advantage. Its learned dynamics transfer to unseen participants, outperforming the linear baseline in 23 of 24 individuals after calibration. While ongoing EEG history accounts for most predictive performance, controlled stimulus analyses reveal an additional video-dependent component. This component also enables evaluation of visual representations, with V-JEPA 2 improving clip-locked prediction by 35% over combined CLIP and DINOv2 features. Our results demonstrate the value of transferable neural dynamics for individual EEG forecasting and highlight the importance of separating state-driven from stimulus-driven predictability.

papers.title_en: Layer-Readout Interfaces in EEG Foundation Models: Predictive Accessibility and Cross-Dataset Transfer
papers.authors: Yanlin Fu, Wei Liu, Liming Zhao
papers.evidence: 研究EEG基础模型跨数据集迁移的预测解码
papers.tldr: 本研究针对EEG基础模型作为冻结特征提取器时中间层优于最终层的现象，分离了读出方式、中间层预测效用和深度结构跨数据集迁移三个因素。在5个模型3个任务上，改进最终层读出可显著恢复性能，但中间层仍有优势；跨5数据集4任务族显示源数据集选出的层可迁移，睡眠分期中任务方向也有效。源选层提供可复用接口，减少目标端搜索并优于最终层基线。
papers.abstract_en: Intermediate layers often outperform final layers when foundation models are used as frozen feature extractors, but the source of this advantage is unclear. We study this question in EEG foundation models by separating three factors: how representations are read out, whether intermediate layers provide predictive utility beyond the final-layer interface, and whether useful depth structure transfers across datasets. Across five models and three tasks, improving the final-layer readout consistently recovers substantial predictive performance, yet intermediate layers remain advantageous within frozen extraction. We also find that layers selected on one dataset remain useful on another across five dataset pairs and four task families, and that a compact set of source-derived task directions retains predictive value after transfer in sleep staging. Together, these results show that predictive utility varies across depth, and its usefulness depends on how representations are read out and transferred. More crucially, source-selected layers provide a reusable feature interface across datasets, reducing the need for target-side layer search while outperforming final-layer baselines on target datasets.

papers.title_en: Is 4 Bits Enough for EEG Sleep Staging? A Subject-Level Benchmark of MXFP4, NVFP4 and FP8
papers.evidence: 对EEG睡眠分期进行量化基准测试，属于时序神经解码任务
papers.tldr: 本研究评估了4位量化格式MXFP4和NVFP4在单通道EEG五阶段睡眠分期中的表现，使用Sleep-EDF-78数据集、受试者交叉验证和精确仿真。结果显示，8/16位量化几乎无损失，而4位量化损失较大，但采用NVFP4格式并在首末层保留FP8精度可使性能接近FP32（差距≤0.48pp），且无需重训练，为可穿戴低功耗睡眠分期提供了实用方案。
papers.abstract_en: Staging sleep on a wearable device keeps the raw electroencephalogram (EEG) private and saves the energy needed to transmit it. It also requires small, energy-efficient neural networks. We benchmark 13 post-training quantization (PTQ) configurations, from FP16 to the block-scaled 4-bit formats MXFP4 and NVFP4, for five-stage sleep staging from single-channel Fpz-Cz EEG. We use Sleep-EDF-78 (78 subjects), subject-wise cross-validation, three training seeds, value-exact emulation, and per-subject paired statistics. All 8- and 16-bit formats stay within 0.45 percentage points (pp) of FP32 Macro-F1. With 4-bit weights and activations, an epoch-wise CNN loses 1.98 to 3.04 pp, and a temporal-context network loses at most 1.19 pp. A same-encoder ablation shows that temporal context explains little of this gap. At equal block size, NVFP4 outperforms MXFP4. The first layer, which quantizes the raw EEG, is the most sensitive layer in both networks. Keeping the first and last layers in FP8 brings both tested 4-bit formats within 0.48 pp of FP32. This recipe adds at most 2.1% weight storage, needs no retraining, and is equivalent to quantization-aware training (QAT) within an exploratory 1-pp margin. The 4-bit losses fall on the same subjects across architectures (Spearman correlation coefficient = 0.69 to 0.79), and they reduce N3 recall the most. On the nested Sleep-EDF-20 subset, NVFP4 with FP8 first and last layers again stays within 0.25 pp of FP32. Under MXFP4, however, the ranking of the architectures reverses, and FP8 first and last layers do not fully recover two of the three tested models. In our emulation, NVFP4 with FP8 first and last layers thus loses little accuracy without QAT in both cohorts.
